summary: Marek Zvelebil was an archaeology and history scholar who studied at the University of Sheffield from circa 1974 to 1976. He subsequently held a post at the University of Sheffield from circa 1981 to 2011.

Margaret Dornish is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California. She served as an Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).
Margaret Gouin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret J. Pearson is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She pursued her PhD at the University of Washington, studying under Hellmut Wilhelm and Burton Watson, and served as a Visiting Fellow at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1997.

Margaret Mead studied at Barnard College and Columbia University under Franz Boas. Her major career posts included roles at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969), Columbia University (1954–1978), Fordham University (1968–1970), and The New School (circa 1954–1978).

Margaret R. Miles studied at San Francisco State University and the Graduate Theological Union. A scholar of religious studies and history, she held posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and served as dean at the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and also studied under postdoctoral mentor Xiuping Hong.
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under her master's supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010) and teacher Karin Preisendanz.

Margarita Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies after studying at Saint Petersburg State University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts. She served at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2021) and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1982–2005).

Maria Heim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey. She served as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Marian Ury was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in circa 1953. She served as a professor at the University of California, Davis from 1969 to 1995.

Marianne Pieper studied at the University of Hamburg and completed her Habilitation at Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. She held posts at the University of Kassel (1994–1996) and the University of Hamburg (1990–1994; professor of sociology 1996–2015).

Marianne Winder studied at the University of London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove. A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, she served at the Wellcome Institute as Assistant Librarian (~1963–1978), Curator (1970), and Consultant (1978).
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and was taught by Sengaku Mayeda.

Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her PhD at Columbia University in 2006 under Robert A. F. Thurman. She also studied under Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, John Stratton Hawley, and Chopathar Wayemache.

Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He held posts at Hampshire College (attested 2001) and as an assistant professor at Rollins College.

Mario Poceski earned his PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, his appointments include the University of Iowa (2001) and Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies and Chinese Religions at the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

Mario Praz studied at the University of Bologna (~1915–1918) and the University of Florence (~1918–1920). He later held academic appointments at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1934–1966).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

Marion Meyer is an archaeology and history scholar. She held positions at the German Archaeological Institute (1984–1985), the University of Florida (1996), the University of Bonn (circa 1997–2003), and the University of Vienna (circa 2003–2020).
